title: Degradation Safeguard Credit Fabric and Tenant Grace Proposal
content:
Summary:

This doc proposes a "Degradation Safeguard Credit Fabric" (DSCF) — an orthogonal soft-layer that sits between Dedicated pool autoscaling and tenant request admission to enable predictable, graceful degradation during transient load/infra events. The fabric issues short-lived credits to tenants so they can sustain short bursts or recover from sudden throttling, while preserving isolation and SLOs for high-priority lanes.

Why this problem matters:
- Customers buying Dedicated expect predictable latency and no sudden noisy-neighbor failures when other tenants spike.
- Rigid hard-eviction or immediate preemption creates customer-facing errors; unlimited overcommit creates tail latency/regression risk.
- Existing autoscalers react too slowly for microbursts and rely on coarse prewarm which is costly.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Reduce user-visible 429/500 spikes during short (seconds-to-minutes) transient overloads by >= 60% for tenants with active credits.
- Maintain latency SLOs for premium fidelity lanes by bounding how credits are applied across lanes.
- Keep incremental pod/GPU cost  < +10% compared to current baseline by using credits + soft-degrade before large autoscale ops.
- Provide clear telemetry and runbook hooks so SREs and SEs can reason about incidents.

Non-goals:
- We are not building a full billing/chargeback ledger here — finance can piggyback later.
- Not intended to replace long-term predictive autoscaler features (forecasting).

High level design:
1) Credit Fabric Concept
   - Credit = a short-lived allowance (in compute-seconds-equivalent or request-units) granted to a tenant to allow requests beyond their steady quota during an overload window.
   - Credits are layered: pool-level safety credits (platform-managed), tenant-granted grace credits (allocated by policy), and emergency escape credits (operator-issued).

2) Credit lifecycle
   - Issue: credits are issued automatically from the DSCF when signals indicate transient overload (burst detected, scaling lag, node drain, cross-pool congestion).
   - Consume: request admission checks credit balance; if credits remain, request is accepted and credits decremented by a request cost computed from model, seq_len, and SLO lane.
   - Decay & Expiry: credits have TTLs and exponential decay to avoid long tail hoarding.
   - Replenish: periodic top-ups for tenants that maintain steady healthy usage patterns (configurable by tier).

3) Isolation & Fairness Policies
   - Priority gating: premium lanes (e.g., low-latency) consume a different credit bucket or have stricter per-request costs so they are protected.
   - Fairshare: credits can be weighted by tenant SLA (committed level) and recent utilization; weight floor/ceiling to avoid starvation.
   - Soft-quarantine: tenants that exceed safe depletion rates are funneled into degraded lanes (reduced concurrency, forced sampling or fallback to smaller models).

4) Autoscaler & Routing integration
   - DSCF is advisory to autoscaler: when credits get consumed above threshold, autoscaler is nudged to accelerate instance bring-up; conversely, if credits cover the surge, autoscaler cooldown is delayed to avoid flapping.
   - Routing fallback: DSCF ties into model-variant fallback rules — credit consumption can trigger transparent routing to quantized/cheaper variants for non-premium lanes.

5) Operator controls and emergency modes
   - Manual credit injection via Console / CLI for customers under incident.
   - Global emergency pool: a small operator-managed reservoir to keep critical workloads alive during region-level issues.

APIs and surface area (sketch):
- GET /v1/dedicated/tenants/{id}/credit-status -> balance, TTLs, weight
- POST /v1/dedicated/tenants/{id}/credit-inject -> operator mode only
- Events emitted: credit_issued, credit_consumed, credit_depleted, credit_topup, credit_expired (to telemetry/console)

Admission costing model (simple first pass):
- cost = base_cost(model_size) * (seq_len/512) * lane_multiplier * quant_multiplier
- base_cost and lane_multiplier configured per pool. This keeps per-request accounting lightweight while enabling meaningful admission decisions.

Telemetry & observability:
- Dashboard: per-tenant credit burn rate, top consumers, time-to-depletion distribution, correlation with 429/latency spikes.
- Alerts: credit_burn_rate_high (per-tenant), emergency_pool_low (org-level), credit_leak_detected (unusual non-request drains).
- Integration with existing Console per-route cost breakdown.

Operational runbook (high level steps):
- Detection: on credit_depleted + 429 spike, SRE checks burn rate window and affected tenants via dashboard.
- Contain: optionally inject emergency credits for important tenant(s), or activate soft-quarantine for noisy tenant.
- Remediate: accelerate autoscaler if infra is the limiter; adjust lane costs or edge routing to offload to cheaper variants.
- Postmortem: capture credit issuance events and correlating autoscaler decisions.

Safety & risk considerations:
- Overly-generous credits may mask real capacity issues and delay autoscaling — mitigate with burn-rate-based autoscaler nudges and maximum credit caps.
- Complexity in costing could cause unpredictable credit depletion. Start with a conservative, easy-to-audit cost function.
- Tenant-perceived fairness: need clear communication on what credits are and that they’re not a durable SLA substitute.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- TTL sizing: short TTLs (30s-2m) reduce hoarding but increase churn; longer TTLs ease UX but increase risk. Propose starting at 90s and iterate.
- Cost granularity: request-unit vs compute-seconds — which gives better SLO correlation? Run a 1-week simulator (Linear DED-412).
- Billing: should credits be tied to billing tier or purchased as burst add-on? (finance/REV input required)

Prototype plan and milestones:
- Week 0-2: lightweight simulator + integration test using historical CBs (team: applied-ml + infra) — mock credit issuance rules.
- Week 3-5: minimal admission-check hook + telemetry events (SRE/serving-runtime collaboration).
- Week 6-8: safety packaging: Console view + manual injection + basic soft-quarantine policies.
- Rollout: staged to test pool -> small set of dedicated customers -> general availability.

Next steps (immediate):
- Sync with infra autoscaler owners (Arjun) and runtime team (Lena) to validate latency cost proxy.
- Kickoff simulation ticket (Linear DED-412).
- Draft Console mockups for credit dashboard (Sofia to lead).

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally opinionated. Looking to keep the admission check cheap and the credit logic transparent so we can iterate quickly.
- Please point out edge-cases where credits could be gamed by clients, and any telemetry gaps we should instrument early.

References & links:
- historical incident notes: slack:#incidents thread (see 2024-07-11 region spike)
- related concepts in dedicated backlog: DED-304 (soft-fallbacks), DED-412 (simulator), INFRA PR 789 (autoscaler nudge hooks)
